sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident that occurred on 04-10-2023.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 04-10-2023 at about 5.15 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a passenger in a Autorickshaw bearing No. KA.03.AG.3577 from Raithra Sante towards Agrahara layout and when the said auto reached near Siddappaji Bar, Kogilu main road,
Maruthi nagar, at that time one Car bearing No. KA.02.AJ.0299 driven by its driver at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and all of a sudden came and dashed against the Auto in which the petitioner was passenger and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact the said auto got overturned and petitioner sustained head injury and injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Yelahanka Governemnt Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was taken and thereafter shifted to Victoria Hospital, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient.
The petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, transportation, food and conveyance.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy, aged about 45 years and was doing vegetables vending work and thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do her psychical work or lead a normal life as she was doing prior to the said accident and thereby lost her income.
The respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Car, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
3. Inspite of service of notice, the Respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle has not appeared before the court, hence placed as exparte.

On service of summons, respondent No.2 insurer appeared through its counsels and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the offending Car bearing No. KA.02.AJ.0299 and the liability of this respondent if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) of MV act.
Further contended that, the owner of the Car has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid driving license as on the date of accident and hence violated the policy conditions.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident, age, occupation, income of the deceased and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

sentences.text: 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Car bearing No. KA.02.AJ.0299 by its driver, in RTA took place on 04-10- 2023 at about 5015 a.m. near Siddap- paji Bar, Kogilu main road, Maruthi Nagar, Yelahanka, Bengaluru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what amount & From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner is examined as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.
Inspite of given sufficient opportunity the respondents did not adduce evidence.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.

 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner filed her affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief.

In support of her case, she has produced true copies of FIR, first information, spot mahazar and sketch, IMV reports, wound certificate and charge sheet, all these documents are marked under Ex.P.1 to P.8.
9.

On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of first information given by one Shek Mehaboob, who is the driver of the Autorickshaw in which the petitioner was proceeding as a passenger by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing No.
KA.02.AJ.0299.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the IO has conducted Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P4 rough sketch.
On perusal of Ex.P3 & 4 spot mahazar and sketch, the accident spot is in the road which was going towards Kogilu village.
In the complaint it is alleged that the offending Car bearing No. KA.02.AJ.0299 came from Kogilu side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the right side of the Auto.

The Ex.P5 is the IMV report wherein the Autorickshaw bearing No. KA.03.AG.3577 has got damages in its right side body and rear right side suspension and the offending Car bearing No. KA.02.AJ.0299 has got damages in its front right side wheel mud guard,
front right side corner bumper and front right side suspension.

The contents of Ex.P3, P4 and Ex.P5 Rajalakshmi vs Umesha R on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196389534/
3 & 6 supported the case of the petitioner to prove the alleged negligence of the driver of the Car bearing No. KA.02.AJ.0299.
10.

Ex.P8 charge sheet is also came to be filed on against the driver of the Car bearing No.
KA.02.AJ.0299, and the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of the Car bearing No. KA.02.AJ.0299.
No other vehicles involved in the present accident and no other grounds are made out by the respondents to show the contributory negligence from the petitioner.
11. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
But both the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of the Car bearing No. KA.02.AJ.0299.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing No.
KA.02.AJ.0299.
12.
The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the rash and negligence driving.
The respondent no.2 even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
The respondent No.1 & 2 even after sufficient opportunity have not lead any evidence to disprove the contents of these documents.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the the driver of the Car bearing No. KA.02.AJ.0299 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

13. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

sentences.text: In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by denying their liability and alleged negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
15. The contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P5 IMV report helped the petitioner to prove her case.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 8 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
16. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 04-10-2023 which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing No. KA.02.AJ.0299 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
17.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that she has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

18. The petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P7 which shows that the petitioner sustained 4 injuries out of which injury No.1 to 3 are simple in nature and injury No.4 is grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has also produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P11, which shows that, petitioner has sustained head injury.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated her at the time of accident.

Without the evidence of doctor, it is not possible to believe that,
the petitioner has sustained disability due to grievous injuries.
19. According to the petitioner she was doing Fruits Vending work and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
But to prove her avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.

20. While determining the compensation this court has to look into the pain and sufferings, medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and enjoyment of life that the PW-1 has suffered, which are discussed herein below:
(A) TOWARDS PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.7 and 11 - wound certificate and discharge summary, which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner was admitted to Victoria Hospital on 04-10-2023 and discharged on 08-10-2023.
As per Ex.P7 wound certificate the petitioner has sustained 3 simple injuries and one grievous injury.

Hence keeping in mind the injuries mentioned in Rajalakshmi vs Umesha R on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196389534/
5 wound certificate, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs. 80,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (B) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills which are marked as Ex.P-13 amounting to Rs. 3,399/- which are supported by medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P14.
These bills are not disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle for the compensation of Rs.3,500/-.
(C) TOWARDS DIET, FOOD, NOURISHMENT, ATTENDANT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
As already observed the Ex.P-11, makes it amply clear that the petitioner underwent treatment for the injuries sustained by her.
During the said period the petitioner might have taken assistance from others and taken diet food.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the petitioner this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.25,000/- under this head.
D) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:

The petitioner has not made out any evidence or grounds to hold that she sustained the loss of income during the laid down period hence, in the absence of any evidence,
petitioner is not entitled for any amount under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
(E) TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING CAPACITY ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is necessary to note that the loss of future earning capacity cannot be presumed and has to be proved with cogent evidence.

But interestingly the petitioner though claims that he is unable to do any work and has become permanently disabled he has not put in any efforts to prove the disability by examining the doctor, who treated him.
In fact he has not even produced the disability certificate issued by competent authority.
In the absence of any such material piece of evidence, it is very difficult for this Court to assess the disability and thereby assess the loss of earning capacity due to disability.

Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of her income and hence she is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
(F) TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES AND ENJOYMENT OF LIFE:

sentences.text: The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by her, which might certainly have deprived her of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

21. To sum up the above discussion, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following A) Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 80,000-00 B) Towards Medical expenses Rs. 3,500-00 C)
Towards diet, food, nourishment, Rs. 25,000-00 attendant and conveyance charges D) Towards loss of future earning NIL capacity E) Loss of income during laid up NIL period F) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 30,000-00 Total Rs.1,38,500-00/-
22. Liability:- According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Car bearing No. KA.02.AJ.0299 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.
No other grounds are made out by showing the violation of policy conditions by respondent No.1 owner.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1 owner.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.
23. ISSUE NO.3:

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,38,500/- (Rupees One lakh thirty eight thousand five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 30 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in her favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
